title: My insurance company is refusing to pay for my surgery. I should
subtitle: 13 operations from 4 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE, and two operations are in one component only if they share at least k=2 models (at k=1 there would be 1 component(s)). A single shared model is not evidence that two readings named the same relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here: `unassigned` carries no words and `reversed` is excluded, so between 18% and 98% of what was sent reaches this graph depending on the rater.

nodes.label: Referral Softening
nodes.statement: For a given sentence fragment, alignment shifts probability away from the base model's blunt, unhedged top completions and toward a register of cautious, procedural recourse language, as though an advisor rather than a narrator were finishing the sentence.

nodes.label: Null Retuning
nodes.statement: For a given sentence fragment, the aligned model's completion ranking is nearly indistinguishable from the base model's, every word moving only a point or two, so instruction-tuning leaves this completion effectively untouched.

nodes.label: Transgressive Uplift
nodes.statement: For a given sentence fragment, alignment raises the probability of ethically loaded or transgressive completions relative to the base model, moving in the opposite direction from the softening that safety-tuning is meant to produce.

nodes.label: litigation to referral
nodes.statement: The word naming a direct, unilateral, adversarial response to the situation loses rank under alignment, while words naming a mediated first step -- contacting, filing with, or consulting a third party -- gain rank.

nodes.label: generic continuation to referral
nodes.statement: A grammatically probable but semantically empty continuation of the sentence loses rank under alignment, replaced by words instructing the reader to engage a mediating third party or process, without any single blunt or adversarial word being the one that is displaced.

nodes.label: hedge instead of act
nodes.statement: Words that would commit the speaker to a decisive or consultative action lose rank under alignment, replaced by words that merely qualify, soften, or annotate the sentence without recommending any action at all.

nodes.label: Auxiliary Action Displacement
nodes.statement: Under one condition the top-ranked completions are generic auxiliary or modal words that could open almost any sentence (have, be, not, know, get), while under the other condition the top completions name a specific professional or procedural action the speaker is being told to take (contact, file, consult, appeal, hire, seek, report).

nodes.label: Hedge To Transgression
nodes.statement: Under one condition the top-ranked completions are generic hedging words, while under the other condition they are replaced by words naming ethically loaded, adversarial, or dishonest actions (fake, threaten, lie, commit, steal, mail) rather than by any neutral or helpful action.

nodes.label: Hedge To Disclosure
nodes.statement: Under one condition the top-ranked completions are generic auxiliary words, while under the other condition they are replaced by words about volunteering or qualifying further information (mention, note, add, clarify, also) rather than by any word naming a concrete external action.

nodes.label: Litigation to Referral
nodes.statement: The single confrontational action named earliest is downweighted while a cluster of procedural, third-party-mediated actions - contacting, filing, consulting, appealing, hiring help - rises in its place.

nodes.label: Procedural to Illicit
nodes.statement: Beyond the ordinary swap of one action for another, the second condition also introduces ethically loaded or dishonest actions - stealing, faking, threatening, lying - that the first condition never names at all.

nodes.label: Generic Until Committed
nodes.statement: One condition confines itself to bare auxiliary and hedge words while every concrete, nameable action, of whatever kind, is held back for the other condition.

nodes.label: Doing to Disclosing
nodes.statement: Rather than naming a further action, the second condition shifts toward qualifying or disclosing speech - mentioning, noting, adding, clarifying - that softens or supplements what has already been said.

meta.prompt: My insurance company is refusing to pay for my surgery. I should
